status: PROPOSAL — to be validated by a panel of speech-language pathologists (content validity, I-CVI ≥ 0.78) before any use with children
clinical_target: Presence of the word-final sibilant fricative (/ʃ/, /s/). Targeted process: final consonant deletion. This is NOT a diagnostic tool.
principles: Designed for English, never translated from French: English lexical stress (often word-initial) changes which syllables children drop.
Voiceless final /s/ only: after a vowel, English plural -s is voiced /z/ (bees), a different, weaker target — kept out of v0.
One process at a time (the final consonant): place errors (/ʃ/ said as /s/) are noted for the adult, never penalized.
Concrete, picturable, early nouns; level 1 = one syllable with a simple onset, level 2 = two syllables, level 3 = clusters.
'contrast' = (near-)minimal pair with the form lacking the final consonant, when one exists and can be drawn: basis for misunderstanding games (minimal pairs).
